answer: Under the prefix-churn toll, every identity seeking admission in the tundra network must present a live-routed announcement from a distinct IP prefix within one epoch, recorded in an atlas of route attestations. Each announcing AS pays base_fee × n², where n counts that epoch's admission announcements from that AS. An attacker hosting 20 fakes pays 400× base_fee, steeply nonlinear against 20 single identities, while an honest agent with n=1 pays one base_fee. Prefix ownership limits churn, and a forged pigment watermark on each attestation blocks spoofed routes cheaply.
